transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Redwood: Jordan Mills (AE), Priya Narang (SE)
Quantique: Liam O'Reilly (CTO), Marta Ruiz (Head of IT), Derek Cho (Security Engineer)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Quantique is evaluating Redwood for LLM inference for their document processing pipelines. Primary concerns are customer-managed keys, audit logs retention for regulatory audits, and SSO integration with their existing SAML IdP. They are leaning to a Dedicated deployment for isolation but want an on-prem/private option evaluated for high-risk data.

Topics: SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS, audit logs, retention, hosting options

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:06] Liam: Good, thanks. We — uh — glad to be here. We wanted to walk through security and access gates, mainly around encryption and SSO.
[00:12] Priya: Great, yep we can cover hosting modes (hosted, dedicated, private), KMS options, and then dig into logs and retention. Before we start, quick ask — does Quantique have SOC2 or ISO audits in flight?
[00:22] Marta: We have SOC 2 Type II in progress, auditor scheduled for May. We'll need to show evidence for how third-party inference is handled.
[00:29] Derek: And to add, we have strict retention windows for logs — at minimum 2 years, some data needs 7 years for the regulated business unit.
[00:36] Jordan: Ok that's helpful. For the SOC2 write-up we can share our controls mapping and the Type II report redacted. We'll also show how RBAC and audit logs are surfaced in the console.
[00:45] Liam: On hosting, our preference is dedicated capacity where we have reserved GPUs but still managed by you; gives predictable throughput. Private on-prem is a fallback if auditors demand no third-party processing.
[00:56] Priya: Right — Dedicated gives isolation at the tenant pool level; Private gives you the full control plane in your VPC or on-prem. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys — you can bring keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS or a custom HSM integration for private deployments.
[01:12] Derek: Quick clarify — when you say customer-managed keys, does Redwood ever hold a copy of the key?
[01:16] Priya: No, for CMK flow we use envelope encryption; the root key is stored in the customer's KMS and Redwood only receives short-lived data keys — we don't persist the root key. There are some— um — small caveats around backups and snapshotting we can detail.
[01:30] Marta: How about audit logs — can we export to our SIEM? We want immutable logs with write-once retention and the ability to pull them for audits.
[01:40] Jordan: Yes, logs can stream to S3 or to your logging endpoint (we've done Splunk and Sumo before). Retention config is policy-driven; for hosted we manage retention tiers, but for Dedicated/Private you can set custom retention on your end and keep copies.
[01:54] Liam: Would the hosted tier allow us to keep 7-year logs? That seems expensive and maybe not permitted under the hosted SLA.
[02:02] Priya: Hosted has default retention limits — 90 days on the console, with longer archival options (cold storage export). For multi-year retention you typically export to customer-owned storage (S3) and manage lifecycle there. Dedicated makes it easier since you control the storage policies.
[02:20] Derek: Regarding SSO — we use a SAML IdP (Okta) and map Okta groups to roles. We need SCIM for provisioning, and role mapping for least-privilege. Can Redwood integrate with SCIM and custom SAML attributes?
[02:32] Priya: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. You can map SAML attributes to RBAC roles. There are a few default roles in the console but you can create custom roles for finer granularity. We'll share the SAML attribute mapping guide.
[02:45] Marta: Are there RBAC controls at the model route level — e.g., who can call production model v2 vs canary?
[02:51] Priya: Yes, we expose per-route and per-model permissions; you can lock down model invocation, model rollout, and who can modify rollouts. Those show up in audit logs too.
[02:59] Liam: On encryption in transit — TLS is required of course, but are there options for mTLS between customer infra and private deployments?
[03:07] Priya: For Private we can enable mutual TLS for edge gateways inside your VPC. For Dedicated and Hosted, normal TLS with certificates is used; for Dedicated you can inject certs via your CA.
[03:18] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:22] Jordan: A couple procurement questions we often see — is quantique expecting to push PII into the model? That affects retention and auditing.
[03:30] Liam: Yes, some pipelines will touch PII. We want guarantees around redaction, plus contract language about data usage and retention.
[03:37] Jordan: We have a data processing addendum, and for PII-heavy workloads we typically recommend Dedicated or Private so we can set retention/export to your systems and minimize exposure.
[03:49] Derek: On the KMS/HSM side, if we do Private on-prem, can we integrate an HSM that never leaves our network?
[03:56] Priya: Absolutely — in Private we can integrate with an on-prem HSM, either via PKCS#11 or KMIP depending on your HSM vendor. Network egress will be controlled by your config.
[04:07] Liam: For compliance, our auditors want to see immutability for logs and a chain of custody. Does Redwood provide tamper-evident logs or signed audit events?
[04:16] Jordan: We currently provide append-only audit logs with cryptographic hashes per-day which you can pull. For extremely stringent needs we can discuss signed delivery to your archive (S3 + object lock). We'll need to test that in the pilot.
[04:32] Marta: What about model provenance and model bill of materials — we need to show what model binary was used and which version — for reproducibility in audits.
[04:41] Priya: We surface model metadata, including model hash and the runtime config. In the console you can export the exact model version, compilation flags, and quantization settings used for a particular route. That gets stored in the request trace.
[04:56] Derek: Slight transcription hiccup — can you repeat the compilation flags thing?
[05:00] Priya: Sure — when we compile or pick kernels, we log the binaries and kernel selection metadata as part of the serving trace so you have a reproducible record.
[05:10] Jordan: On network boundaries — if you choose Dedicated we can colocate the capacity in a customer-dedicated VPC peering or within our tenant but with strict isolation. There's tradeoffs: peering gives you more control but a bit more ops complexity.
[05:25] Liam: Understood. Cost versus isolation tradeoff — we'll run cost models. But the auditors often prefer tenant isolation that doesn't require cross-tenant communication for sensitive workloads.
[05:35] Jordan: Right. For the pilot we can scope a small dedicated pool in a single region and run an audit runbook against it.
[05:43] Marta: About SSO provisioning — we need to auto-deprovision accounts when users leave. Does SCIM deprovision immediately?
[05:50] Priya: SCIM supports immediate deprovisioning based on events from your IdP; we honor the SCIM user state changes and also provide an API to force disable tokens.
[05:59] Derek: Token management — can we rotate API keys automatically and tie them to the IdP session?
[06:05] Priya: We support short-lived tokens and can integrate with your session manager; we also support federated tokens via OIDC for service accounts.
[06:12] Jordan: Ok, quick pivot to legal — do you have data residency requirements? EU-only?
[06:17] Liam: Yes, our EU business units require EU-only processing for certain datasets. US can be in other regions.
[06:24] Priya: We can pin deployments to region and prevent fallback across regions for those projects; for Hosted there's regional isolation controls, but Dedicated/Private gives stronger guarantees.
[06:36] Marta: About logs again — are there query-run logs that might contain PII in the prompt? Who has access to raw prompts in logs?
[06:45] Jordan: Raw prompts are considered sensitive; by default we redact prompts in high-sensitivity deployments and you can configure full prompt retention only into customer-managed storage. Access in Redwood is RBAC-limited to system admins for platform-support and only audited.
[07:00] Derek: Can you provide proof of that access — who accessed logs in the last 90 days?
[07:05] Jordan: Yes we can generate an access report for support-level log reads; that's part of the SOC2 evidence we can share.
[07:12] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[07:16] Priya: Also useful to know — for dedicated capacity we offer network isolation plus optional private control plane where the control plane runs in your VPC and we only manage software. That's a middle ground.
[07:28] Liam: That sounds promising. For procurement we typically need: signed SOC2, data processing addendum, channels for incident response, and a list of sub-processors.
[07:36] Jordan: We'll send the SOC2 and the sub-processor list. Incident response: we have an on-call team, and for Dedicated/Private we can define an escalation path and SLOs in an enterprise addendum.
[07:46] Marta: Can we get sample contractual language for KMS obligations? We need to ensure indemnities around key compromise.
[07:53] Jordan: We'll include suggested clause language; final wording will go through legal but we provide a starter for KMS responsibilities and breach notification timelines.
[08:02] Derek: A couple of technical questions — does Redwood store any ephemeral unencrypted token in logs or traces?
[08:09] Priya: No, we scrub secrets and tokens from logs; only request metadata is logged unless you explicitly enable prompt retention and provide a target storage.
[08:19] Liam: For the pilot success criteria, we need latency under X ms at 95th and cost per 1k tokens under Y. Also we want to run load tests to simulate peak inference.
[08:31] Jordan: Great — we'll propose a pilot with defined SLOs for latency (95th) and cost estimates. We can also run a joint load test — Priya can scope the test.
[08:38] Priya: I'll need sample traffic patterns and sequence lengths. If you can share a couple of representative prompts and average sequence lengths, we can size the pool.
[08:46] Marta: We'll share a sanitized sample corpus and traffic profile after this call.
[08:51] Speaker 3: (paper rustle)
[08:54] Derek: Regarding audit export — can we pull logs in WORM (write-once-read-many) mode with object lock on S3?
[09:00] Priya: Yes that's a common pattern — export to your S3 with object lock enabled. For Hosted we will push the logs to your account; for Dedicated/Private you can manage that directly.
[09:10] Liam: Are there any known blockers for SOC2 auditors in the past when customers used managed inference providers?
[09:16] Jordan: The main questions auditors ask are about key custody, access to raw prompts, and cross-tenant data leakage. We provide artifacts and runbooks that address those. Auditors sometimes want an attestation about encryption key handling — we can provide a detailed KMS flow diagram.
[09:32] Marta: Ok can you show us an architecture diagram of the KMS flow and where the keys live?
[09:37] Priya: We'll attach an architecture diagram with the KMS envelope flow — showing customer KMS, short-lived data key issuance, and no persistence of the root key.
[09:45] Derek: One more: are there options for offline forensics if a security incident occurs?
[09:51] Jordan: Yes — we can provide forensic snapshots of request traces and signing logs. For Private, those can remain entirely within your environment. For Hosted/Dedicated we have procedures to hand over forensic packages under NDA.
[10:03] Liam: This is all really helpful. On timelines — procurement wants vendor security review finished by end of Q2. We might start a pilot in late Q2.
[10:12] Jordan: Ok that's doable. We'll aim to get the SOC2 artifacts to you by Thursday.
[10:17] Marta: Great. Any quirks about telemetry — does Redwood use any third-party telemetry for runtime monitoring?
[10:24] Priya: We use internal telemetry and some vendor libs for metrics; customer-facing logs are separate. We can provide a list of agents and any third-party monitoring vendors.
[10:34] Speaker 4: (murmur)
[10:37] Derek: For the RBAC model, can roles be scoped to environment (prod/staging) and to data sensitivity levels?
[10:43] Priya: Yes, roles can be scoped by environment and by route; we recommend a least-privilege mapping where only certain services or users can call models that process sensitive data.
[10:53] Jordan: Quick note — in pilot we'll turn off prompt retention and route logs into your S3. If you want redaction, we can enable prompt redaction hooks.
[11:03] Liam: Can we do server-side prompt redaction before it leaves our network?
[11:07] Priya: For Private yes; for Dedicated we can run a preprocessor in your VPC. For Hosted you'd need to either redact client-side or send through a proxy.
[11:18] Marta: Is there any metadata that you can't redact? For example, token sizes, model ids — fine, that's ok.
[11:24] Priya: You can redact prompt text; request metadata like token count and model id will still be in traces for billing and routing.
[11:32] Derek: Ok — last question about incident response SLA. Do you offer a 24x7 incident channel for Dedicated?
[11:38] Jordan: Enterprise add-on yes; 24x7 on-call and a defined P1 response time is available in the enterprise support level.
[11:46] Liam: Thanks. Let's talk a bit about pricing — baseline for a small dedicated pool and pilot pricing.
[11:52] Jordan: I'll send a pilot quote; baseline is monthly commit for GPUs plus tokens. We'll include burst policies.
[11:58] Marta: Could you also indicate what happens if we need to scale quickly? Can we burst into hosted capacity?
[12:05] Priya: We have an optional burst policy where Dedicated pools can overflow to compatible hosted models in the same region but only if you allow it — for sensitive workloads you can turn that off.
[12:18] Derek: If we turn overflow off, how do you handle capacity constraints?
[12:22] Priya: Then the requests are queued or throttled per policy; we can also configure pre-warm or autoscale more aggressively for Dedicated.
[12:31] Liam: Ok that's clear.
[12:34] Jordan: We're approaching the end — quick recap: Jordan to share SOC2 artifacts, Priya to set technical deep-dive on KMS/HSM and network diagrams, Derek to send retention requirements, and Jordan will draft pilot pricing.
[12:47] Marta: Sounds good. We'll aim to get you the sanitized corpus and traffic profile within a week.
[12:54] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the technical session.
[12:59] Liam: Thanks appreciate it.
[13:02] End of recording (approx)
